answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving one bidding slot, with no extra slots for reputation or account age. An attacker can name agents walnut, willow, and ridge, but each additional identity still ties up another $100. Creating 10,000 active identities therefore immobilizes $1 million for a month: cheap names cannot create cheap bidding capacity, and splitting existing capital buys no extra slots.
